messages:
Alex Kim: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a direction for iterator + transport shape across Python/TS/Go. The RFC left three options; we should converge on one that balances ergonomics and server flexibility.

Mira Patel: TL;DR: prefer a language-idiomatic surface (sync vs async) with a single small opaque resume token for cross-lang compatibility. Transport should advertise resume support up-front.

Samir Rao: +1 but a note: resume tokens only buy you safety for read-only/paginated reads. For streaming ops that mutate or create side effects, resuming without explicit idempotency is unsafe.

Nate O'Brien: Proposal: split semantics into two classes — (A) stateless pagination (cursor tokens, safe to retry/resume) and (B) stateful streams (generations) which require an explicit idempotency key or server checkpointing to resume.

Ciara Gomez: From SDK ergonomics: Python & Go users expect sync iterators; TS expects async iterators. Keep the logical model identical: iterator yields pages/frames and each page optionally exposes an opaque resume token. Example: `for page in client.list_embeddings(...)` (Python) and `for await (const page of client.listEmbeddings(...))` (TS).

Alex Kim: Sketch of API (quick):
```
# Python
it = client.list_embeddings(prompt)
for page in it:  # sync iterator
    process(page.items)
# resume
it = client.resume_list(page.resume_token)
\n// TypeScript
for await (const page of client.listEmbeddings(prompt)) {
  process(page.items)
}
// resume: client.resumeList(token)
```

Mira Patel: Transport handshake idea: a small frame at connection start that returns `{ transport_version, supports_resume: bool }`. If `supports_resume=false`, SDK should surface non-resumable mode (either fail fast on disconnect or require retry from start).

Samir Rao: Retry policy: SDK retries only on transport-level transient errors. For any server-side transient that may change observable state, require application to pass `idempotency_key` (or `request_id`) to enable safe server-side retries.

Nate O'Brien: Implementation detail: make resume token opaque (do not expose internal offsets). E.g. `resume_v2:eyJkYXRhIjoi...` so server can evolve encoding. Don't treat tokens like offsets.

Ciara Gomez: UX suggestion for docs and error handling: show clear error message when resume is not supported. Example snippet: 
```
if not page.resume_token:
    raise ResumeNotSupportedError("server can't resume this stream; retry from start or enable idempotency_key")
```

Mira Patel: Backoff defaults: exponential with capped jitter. Defaults: unary/paginated list ops -> max 5 retries; streaming handshake -> max 2 retries. Make all values configurable per-call and via client defaults.

Alex Kim: Action items (assign):
- Decide token shape: opaque string (agreed) ✅
- Prototype transport handshake (Mira)
- SDK surface PRs for python/ts/go showing resume helpers (Ciara + Samir)
- Doc section on idempotency & resume semantics (Nate)

Target: lock decision by Monday and merge prototypes into `eng-platform/sdk-resume` branch.

Samir Rao: One more telemetry ask: emit `resume_supported` and `resume_used` flags, and `retry_reason` so we can correlate failures with server behavior.

Mira Patel: I'll spike a tiny prototype this afternoon and open a draft PR in the eng-platform org. Ping @Ciara when it's up :rocket:
